notes: Willard E. Worden's glass plate negatives. The addressed half of the collection is two residence parks being built — Ingleside Terraces and Jordan Park, photographed house by house between 1911 and 1915, four plates of them still under construction — plus seven flats on 8th and 9th Avenues in the Inner Richmond. 330 of the 433 records give no street number and are not kept as findings (COLLECTION_UNNUMBERED_POLICY in digitalsf_extract.py): they are the photographer's miscellany, Camp McCoy and Y.M.C.A. portraits and views across Brisbane. Caption tails are the owner about as often as anything — "Residence of Mrs. Henrietta Lehe, 15 Cerritos Avenue" — so the collection reads under named-buildings-only and keeps no name at all; all 21 owners are dropped at extraction, per "Privacy — hard limits" in the root AGENTS.md. Two addresses printed as the second house in a caption were added by hand, since the extractor takes the first address it can parse.

coverage.remaining: None — the collection was read whole.
coverage.note: 433 records read; 330 give no street number and are not kept; one is a photograph of people with no address; 102 give a number and fold into 77 findings, plus two second addresses and one construction credit added by hand, over 66 distinct addresses. 72 reached a parcel and 8 did not — 4 because the number no longer exists in EAS, 3 because a two-number flat address is now two parcels, and one because EAS has the address but joins it to no parcel. 60 published on 59 pages, 50 of them seeded for it; 12 declined, 11 as a second plate of the same house at a vaguer date and one as a credit the page already carried from the OMI context statement.
